title: Half-life: how radioactive material decays
examples: How much is left after three half-lives?

marks.ask: How do you calculate what is left after several half-lives?

explain.say: Imagine 800 popcorn kernels in a hot pan. You cannot tell which kernel will pop next, but you can say that half will pop in a certain time. Radioactive atoms are like that. Each one decays, or breaks down, at random. Let us watch a sample.

marks.label: 18 h: 100 left
marks.ask: How do you calculate what is left after several half-lives?

explain.say: Look at the graph. We start with 800 atoms of technetium, a substance doctors use for scans. See the first dot? After 6 hours, half have decayed, so 400 are left. That time, 6 hours, is the half-life. How many are left?

marks.label: 18 h: 100 left
marks.ask: How do you calculate what is left after several half-lives?

explain.say: 400, yes! Now another 6 hours. Half of 400 is 200. Look at the second dot. Each half-life, the amount halves again. That is why the curve drops fast and then more and more slowly. After 12 hours, how many are left?

marks.label: 18 h: 100 left
marks.ask: How do you calculate what is left after several half-lives?

explain.say: 200, perfect! After 18 hours, three half-lives, half of 200 leaves 100. The sum is: start, then halve, halve, halve. So 800, 400, 200, 100. Will it ever reach exactly zero?

marks.label: 18 h: 100 left

explain.say: Not quite, it just keeps halving, great thinking! Doctors like a 6 hour half-life: long enough for a scan, then it fades away. Wow fact: carbon-14 has a half-life of about 5730 years, so scientists use it to date ancient bones and wood. Challenge: 1600 atoms, after 4 half-lives?

faq.a: Half-life is the time it takes for half of the radioactive atoms in a sample to decay, or for its activity to halve.

faq.q: How do you calculate what is left after several half-lives?
faq.a: Halve the amount once for every half-life. 800 atoms after three half-lives is 800, 400, 200, then 100.

faq.a: You cannot predict when one particular nucleus will decay, but with huge numbers of atoms the overall rate is very predictable.
asks: Can you predict when an atom will decay?

faq.q: How do you find half-life from a graph?
faq.a: Read the starting value, find half of it on the vertical axis, go across to the curve and down to the time axis.
Living things take in carbon-14. After death it decays with a half-life of about 5730 years, so measuring what is left tells us the age.
